llc-meeting-minutes-template.0: LLC owners search for an LLC meeting minutes template for 2 reasons. Either a bank, lender or accountant asked for minutes, or they read that keeping them helps protect their personal liability. Both are good reasons to get the basics right.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.1: Covered here: whether LLCs need minutes, what to include, and copy-ready templates for annual meetings, first meetings and single-member LLCs.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.2: In most US states, the law does not require an LLC to hold annual meetings or keep minutes, unlike corporations. Your operating agreement can, though. If it does, you must follow it. Some lenders, investors and banks also ask for minutes or resolutions before acting.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.4: Hold and record at least 1 meeting a year, and record any major decision when it happens. Got a schedule in your operating agreement? Follow that.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.7: A single-member LLC has 1 owner and no one else to meet with, so the usual approach is a written consent or resolution signed by the sole member. That records the decision the same way minutes would.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.9: Usually held within weeks of filing, the first meeting (sometimes called the organizational meeting) records the setup decisions after you form the LLC. Typical resolutions include:
llc-meeting-minutes-template.10: List these as numbered resolutions in the main template above. Registered agent services such as [Northwest Registered Agent](https://www.northwestregisteredagent.com/legal-forms/llc/first-meeting-minutes) also publish free first-meeting forms.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.11: Yes, slightly. Member-managed LLCs record meetings of their members. A manager-managed LLC usually records 2 kinds of meetings: manager meetings for day-to-day decisions, and member meetings for the decisions the operating agreement reserves to members, such as admitting new members or selling the business.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.14: Keep discussion summaries short. What matters later is the resolutions and votes.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.15: Store LLC minutes with your other company records: the articles of organization, operating agreement, member list and tax filings. A dedicated folder, physical or digital, with signed PDFs works well. Some states require LLCs to keep certain records at their principal office, so check your state's rules.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.16: How long? For the life of the company. Storage costs nothing, and minutes can matter years later during a sale, audit or dispute.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.17: AI can capture a members' meeting and draft the discussion summary, decisions and action items, so you only check resolution wording and votes before signing. Especially handy for multi-member LLCs that meet on video calls.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.18: More formats: our [meeting minutes sample](https://lynkk.ai/blog/meeting-minutes-sample) and [board meeting agenda template](https://lynkk.ai/blog/board-meeting-agenda).
llc-meeting-minutes-template.19: Most states do not legally require LLCs to keep minutes, but your operating agreement may, and minutes help document major decisions and support liability protection. Banks, lenders and buyers often ask for minutes or resolutions before approving a loan or a sale. Keeping them saves time later.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.20: Hold at least one annual meeting and record it, plus record major decisions as they happen. Follow any schedule in your operating agreement. Single-member LLCs can sign one annual written consent for the year's major decisions, with separate ones for big one-off actions.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.21: Usually it is a written consent signed by the sole member, listing resolutions for the year or for a specific decision. That document records the decision the same way minutes would. Banks often ask to see it before opening an account or approving credit.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.22: Usually the person who chaired the meeting and the person who recorded the minutes sign. Single-member LLC? The sole member signs a written consent. Use a printed name, signature and date for each signer, and keep the signed copy with the operating agreement and other company records.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.23: Admitting members, changing ownership, taking significant debt, buying or selling major assets, opening bank accounts, amending the operating agreement and electing managers. Record each one as a resolution with exact wording and the vote. Why the precision? Banks, buyers and courts will rely on that wording later.
